takeaway: Type II (cytotoxic) hypersensitivity: IgG and IgM bind antigens on the patient's own cells and activate the classical complement pathway. Examples: ABO incompatibility, autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.

lines.text: Type Two hypersensitivity is also called tissue-specific, or cytotoxic, hypersensitivity.
Here, antibodies bind to antigens on the patient's own cell surfaces.
Which mediator is it? Immunoglobulin G.
IgG and IgM antibodies bind these antigens, forming complexes.
lines.say: I g G and I g M antibodies bind these antigens, forming complexes.

lines.text: These activate the classical pathway of complement, to eliminate the cells presenting the antigens.
Examples include ABO blood incompatibility and autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.
lines.say: Examples include A B O blood incompatibility and autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.

lines.text: So for Type Two, the answer is immunoglobulin G.
